title: KINETIC
summary: Labor and interruption — coordinated work rhythms broken by maintenance and rest. Make a passage from three documented work processes. Establish a repeated movement in each, briefly coordinate their rhythms through a sound phrase, break that coordination with one complete maintenance/waiting interval at normal speed, widen to context, and end when a mechanism stops. Cut across 7 verified public-domain archival windows (48.7s) and audited across two Critic Tribunal rounds (v1 → v2).

reviews.text:
VERDICT: pass (Round 1 — v1 assembly audit)
Critic Role: Independent systems critic

Observed Defects on v1 Proof Strip:
- Optional v2 enhancement — Seg #05 (t=18.60s-23.80s): Upgrade 'THREE WORKSHOPS ALIGNED' from a single-stream shot to a synchronized 3-panel triptych locking Processes 01, 02, and 03 visually to the pulse.

Largest Gap:
All v1 shots were clean and cut-free; upgrading Seg #05 to a 3-panel triptych makes the three-workshop rhythmic coordination visually explicit.

Causal Hypothesis:
Single-stream segment mode used in v1 for Seg #05.

Falsifiable Repair Condition:
Use `mode='triptych'` with `clips=['6ee8ef44', '9b8b1f1e', 'aeebdc87']` in Seg #05 so watchmaking, loom shuttle, and factory stamping lock together visually before the normal-speed maintenance interruption (`2ab95576`).

Strength to Preserve:
All three work processes, the normal-speed bearing-oiling maintenance interruption (`2ab95576`), the wide factory-floor contextual reveal (`eba7d1c4`), and the worker stopping at the close (`135e3a64`).
